OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Groq, Together, vLLM, Ollama, or a gateway of your own.

headers.description: Headers for the model call — where the API key goes.

system.description: System prompt, prepended as the first message.

input.description:
The conversation. Either a plain string (becomes one user message) or an array of
`{role, content}` objects — the shape a chat UI already holds.

tools.description: Interfaces in THIS config to offer as tools, by name.

mcp.description:
Remote MCP servers to draw tools from, in addition to `tools`.

Their tools are discovered at run time via `tools/list`, so the model is offered
whatever the server currently publishes — no second copy of the schema to maintain
here. A name that collides with another tool is refused rather than shadowed.

max_iterations.description:
How many model round trips the loop may take. Default 4, hard ceiling 12.

This is the bound that makes an agent safe to expose: each iteration is a model
call plus every tool it asked for, and a model that keeps calling tools would
otherwise run until something else stopped it. Reaching the budget is reported,
never silent.

memory.description:
Remember this conversation across requests.

Without it an agent starts every request with an empty history: it cannot answer "and
what about tomorrow?" because it never saw yesterday's question. With it, the last
exchanges for a session are replayed into the next call.

## Example
```yaml
memory:
  key: a|body::session_id|   # what makes one conversation distinct from another
  window: 10                 # how many past messages to replay
  ttl: 24h                   # how long a silent conversation survives
```

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, passed through when set.

timeout.description: Seconds to allow each model call. Default 60.

headers.description: Headers for every call to it — where its credential goes.

only.description:
Offer only these of the server's tools. Absent means all of them.

Worth setting deliberately: a remote server decides what it publishes, so without a
list the model's abilities change when somebody else edits their config.

AgentMemory.description:
Air Pipe interface definition. An interface represents an endpoint that can be
invoked (via HTTP, schedule, etc.) and executes a chain of actions.

## Example
```yaml
myApiEndpoint:              # Interface name (can be used as route path)
  summary: Get users        # Short description for documentation
  description: |            # Long description (optional)
    Retrieves a list of all
    users in the organization.
  method: POST              # HTTP method (for HTTP interfaces)
  route: /users             # URL path (optional, defaults to interface name)
  tags:                     # OpenAPI tags for grouping
    - Users
    - API
  output: http              # Output type: http

  templates:                # Interface-specific response templates
    success_template: |
      { "status": "ok" }

  actions:                  # Ordered list of actions to execute
    - name: ValidateJwt     # Action name (used for references)
        input: a|headers    # Input source (a|headers, a|body, etc.)
      - name: FetchData
        database: main      # Database connection to use, assuming global is defined
        query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE org_uuid = $1
        params:
          - a|CheckBody::organization_uuid|

  assert:                   # Final assertion against action results
    tests:
      - value: count()
        is_equal_to: 1

  response:                 # Response configuration
    http_code_on_error: 400 # HTTP status code on error
    http_code_inherit_error: [FetchData]  # Inherit error code from action
```
Field defaults an interface hands to every action it contains.

The outcome of an action is DECLARED (`expect_status` / `expect_exit`), never inferred from
an assert. Declaring it per action is right for a pipeline where each call has its own
contract, and tedious for an interface where they share one — a test runner asserting on the
status of thirty routes under test, a health-check fan-out that records whatever it gets. So
the interface can say it once and each action may still override it.

Resolved at config load (see `IntegrationConfig::compile_expressions`), so the interpreter
and the compiled fast path both see a plain action-level value and the request path pays
nothing for it.

## Example
```yaml
interfaces:
  tests/all:
    defaults:
      expect_status: any        # the statuses ARE what this interface tests
    actions: [...]
```
Conversation memory for an `agent:` action.

key.description:
What makes one conversation distinct from another — a session id, a chat id, a user id.

Usually a marker: `a|body::session_id|`. There is no default on purpose. A shared
constant would put every caller's conversation in one history, which leaks one user's
messages into another user's prompt.

window.description:
How many stored messages to replay. Defaults to 10, capped at 50.

Every replayed message is sent to the model on every call, so a larger window means a
larger prompt. Whether that fits — and what it costs — depends on the model this agent
is pointed at, which is yours to choose.

ttl.description: How long a conversation survives without activity, e.g. `24h`, `7d`. Defaults to 24h.

namespace.description: State namespace to store under. Defaults to the config name.

CodeAction.description:
Run JavaScript over this action's input.

Accepts either the script on its own, or the script plus options.

## Example
```yaml
- name: Normalise
  code: |
    return items.map(i => ({ json: { id: i.json.id, total: i.json.amount * 1.1 } }));
```

anyOf.description: Just the script, with every option left at its default.

CodeConfig.description:
The long form of a `code:` action.

## Example
```yaml
- name: Normalise
  code:
    source: |
      const rate = 1.1;
      return items.map(i => ({ json: { id: i.json.id, total: i.json.amount * rate } }));
    mode: all_items
    input: a|FetchOrders|
    timeout_ms: 5000
    memory_bytes: 33554432
```

source.description:
The script.

It is wrapped in an async function, so `await` works at the top level and the value you
`return` becomes the action's output.

Markers in the script are **not** substituted. Splicing request data into a program's
text is code injection — the reason database parameters are bound rather than
concatenated — so data reaches the script as data, through `items` and the bindings.

mode.description:
Whether the script sees every item at once, or runs once per item.

Defaults to `all_items`.

input.description:
What becomes `items`. Any marker resolving to an array or an object.

Defaults to the previous action's data, which is what `input:` does everywhere else.

timeout_ms.description:
Wall-clock budget for one execution, in milliseconds.

Enforced by an interrupt handler rather than a timer, so a script that never yields is
still stopped. Capped by the organisation's `max_script_ms` entitlement — asking for
more than the ceiling gets the ceiling, it is not an error.

memory_bytes.description:
Heap ceiling for one execution, in bytes.

An allocation past this fails the action rather than the process. Capped by the
organisation's `max_script_memory_bytes` entitlement.

language.description: Which language the source is written in. Only `js` today.

dependencies.description:
Packages this script may import, as name to version range.

```yaml
code:
  dependencies:
    date-fns: ^3.6.0
  source: |
    const { format } = require("date-fns");
```

A script that imports something runs in the script runtime rather than the embedded
interpreter, and can only reach what is declared here — nothing else is fetched, and
nothing is resolved while a request is in flight.

Declared per action rather than per config so that what a script may reach is visible
beside the script itself, which is also where a reviewer looks for it.

CodeMode.description: How the script sees its input.

oneOf.description: The script runs once. `items` is the whole array, and it returns an array.
The script runs once per item, with `item` and `$json` bound to that item.

CodeLanguage.description: The language a `code:` action is written in.

oneOf.description: JavaScript.

Assert.description:
Assertion block for validating action output or interface results.
Groups one or more tests with shared error handling and HTTP response codes.

## Example - Action-level assertion
```yaml
actions:
  - name: ValidateBody
    input: a|body|
    assert:
      tests:
        - value: email
          is_not_empty: true
          regex: "^[^@]+@[^@]+\\.[^@]+$"
        - value: age
          data_type: Number
          is_greater_than: 0
      error_message: "Validation failed"
      http_code_on_error: 400
```

## Example - Interface-level assertion
```yaml
interfaces:
  getUser:
    method: GET
    actions:
      - name: FetchUser
        database: main
        query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1
        params:
          - a|params::id|
    assert:
      tests:
        - value: count()
          is_equal_to: 1
      error_message: "User not found"
      http_code_on_error: 404
      http_code_on_success: 200
```

error_message.description:
Message returned when any test fails. Overrides individual test error messages
at the assert level.

http_code_on_error.description:
HTTP status code to return when any test fails. Individual test-level
`http_code_on_error` takes precedence when set.

http_code_on_success.description: HTTP status code to return when all tests pass.

tests.description:
List of test definitions to evaluate. All tests run concurrently;
errors from all tests are collected and returned together.

## Example
```yaml
tests:
  - value: username
    is_not_empty: true
    error_message: "Username is required"
    http_code_on_error: 422
  - value: password
    is_not_empty: true
    contains_upper: true
    contains_number: true
    data_type: String
    is_greater_than: 7
```

rename_attributes.description:
Rename attributes (keys) within a JSON object. Maps old attribute names to new attribute names.

## Example
```yaml
rename_attributes:
  old_name: new_name
```

remove_attributes.description:
Remove specified attributes from the JSON object. Provides an array of attribute names to exclude.

## Example
```yaml
remove_attributes:
  - password
  - secret
```

keep_attributes.description:
Keep only specified attributes, removing all others. Provides an allowlist of attribute names.

## Example
```yaml
keep_attributes:
  - id
  - name
  - email
```

move_attributes.description:
Move attributes from one location to another. Maps source path to destination path.

## Example
```yaml
move_attributes:
  user.name: name
  user.email: email
```

rename_keys.description:
Rename keys at the root level of a JSON object. Maps old key names to new key names.

## Example
```yaml
rename_keys:
  user_id: userId
  created_at: createdAt
```

remove_keys.description:
Remove specified keys from the JSON object. Provides an array of key names to exclude.

## Example
```yaml
remove_keys:
  - token
  - internal_id
```

bcrypt.description:
Hash a value using bcrypt for secure password storage. Supports custom cost factor.

## Example
```yaml
bcrypt:
  key: password          # Path to the password value (e.g., .password)
  cost: 12               # Cost factor (higher = slower but more secure)
```

add_attribute.description:
Add new attributes to the JSON object with specified key-value pairs.

## Example
```yaml
add_attribute:
  user_uuid: a|uuid|           # Auto-generate UUID
  verification_token: a|uuid|  # Auto-generate token
```

return_row.description:
Return a specific row from a result set by index (0-based).

## Example
```yaml
return_row: 0    # Return the first row
```

extract_value.description:
Extract a single value from the response using a JSON path.

## Example
```yaml
extract_value: .user.id
```

extract_array.description:
Extract an array from a JSON response with options for flattening and deduplication.

## Example
```yaml
extract_array:
  from: .items         # Path to the array
  paths:               # Paths to extract from each element
    - id
    - name
  flatten: true        # Flatten nested arrays
  dedupe: true         # Remove duplicates
```

extract_with_json_path.description:
Extract data using a JSON path expression. Shortcut for simple extractions.

## Example
```yaml
extract_with_json_path: .[0]  # Get first element
```

extract_with_jq.description:
Extract data using jq filter syntax for complex JSON transformations.

## Example
```yaml
extract_with_jq: '.users | map({id, name})'
```

extract_with_regex.description:
Extract values from a string using regex capture groups.

## Example
```yaml
extract_with_regex:
  value: .phone                           # Path to source string
  expr: "(\\d{3})-(\\d{3})-(\\d{4})"   # Regex with capture groups
  keys:                                   # Names for captured groups
    - area
    - prefix
    - number
```

extract_with_css.description:
Extract values from an HTML document with a CSS selector — the counterpart to
`extract_with_jq` for pages instead of JSON. Point `value` at the HTML string
(usually an http action's body) and the result lands under `key`.

## Example
```yaml
extract_with_css:
  value: ""                      # the whole action data is the HTML string
  selector: "article h2.title"
  key: titles
  all: true                      # every match, not just the first
```

compress.description:
Compress a value with gzip/zlib/deflate and store it as text.

CPU-bound, so on AirPipe-hosted infrastructure it is gated by the `compression`
entitlement per organization; a self-hosted agent spends its own CPU and is on by
default. Both are additionally bounded by `max_compress_bytes` (8 MiB default).

## Example
```yaml
compress:
  value: rows          # what to compress ("" = the whole action data)
  key: packed
  algorithm: gzip      # gzip (default) | zlib | deflate
  encoding: base64     # base64 (default) | base64url | hex
```

decompress.description:
The inverse of `compress`. Same entitlement and the same byte bound, which here
bounds the OUTPUT too — a small archive that expands past the limit is refused
rather than expanded.

## Example
```yaml
decompress:
  value: packed
  key: rows
  algorithm: gzip
  json: true           # parse the result as JSON instead of keeping it as text
```

totp.description:
Generate the current RFC 6238 one-time password for a shared secret — for calling an
upstream API that demands a second factor. The verifying counterpart is the
`is_valid_totp` assertion.

## Example
```yaml
totp:
  secret: a|secret::vendor::totp_seed|
  key: otp
```

parse_xlsx.description:
Read a spreadsheet (`.xlsx`/`.xls`/`.ods`) that arrived as base64 into rows.

CPU- and memory-bound on a file somebody else produced, so on AirPipe-hosted
infrastructure it is gated by the `document_parsing` entitlement and bounded by
`max_document_bytes` (16 MiB default). Self-hosted is on by default.

## Example
```yaml
parse_xlsx:
  value: file          # base64 of the workbook
  key: rows
  sheet: Orders        # optional — the first sheet otherwise
  limit: 5000          # optional row cap (default 10000)
```

parse_pdf.description:
Extract the text of a PDF that arrived as base64. Same entitlement and byte bound
as `parse_xlsx`.

## Example
```yaml
parse_pdf:
  value: file
  key: text
```

add_jwt.description:
Add a JWT token to the response with configurable expiration and payload.

## Example
```yaml
add_jwt:
  key: jwt                               # Output key for the token
  secret: a|var::JWT_SECRET|            # JWT secret (use encrypted variable)
  exp: 1d                                # Expiration STRING (e.g., 1h, 1d, 30m)
  data:                                  # Claims — three accepted forms:
    sub: a|FetchUser::id|                #  • object: explicit claim -> value (most flexible)
    email: a|FetchUser::email|
  # data: [id, email]                    #  • array: copy these fields from this action's input
  # data: all                            #  • "all": copy every input field
```

**Security:** Store JWT secrets as encrypted AirPipe variables:
```yaml
secret: a|var::ENCRYPTED_JWT_SECRET|
```

read_jwt.description:
Read and decode a JWT token to extract its payload.

## Example
```yaml
read_jwt:
  key: user_data       # Output key for decoded payload
  token: .auth_header  # Path to JWT token
```

numerics.description:
Convert string fields to numeric types. Provides an array of field names to convert.

## Example
```yaml
numerics:
  - age
  - price
  - quantity
```

group_by.description:
Group array elements by specified fields. Used for aggregation operations.

## Example
```yaml
group_by:
  - category
  - region
```

generate_password.description:
Generate a secure random password with customizable options for length and character types.

## Example
```yaml
generate_password:
  key: temp_password         # Output key for generated password
  length: 16                 # Password length
  numbers: true              # Include numbers (0-9)
  lowercase_letters: true    # Include lowercase (a-z)
  uppercase_letters: true    # Include uppercase (A-Z)
  symbols: true              # Include symbols (!@#$)
```

replace_values.description:
Replace values in strings or arrays with support for regex and multiple replacements.

## Example - Simple string replacement
```yaml
replace_values:
  target_value: .message    # Path to target value
  find_str: old             # String to find
  new_str: new              # Replacement string
```

## Example - Multiple value replacement
```yaml
replace_values:
  target_value: .status
  values:                    # Array of values to process
    - pending
    - approved
  find_str: _
  new_str: " "
```

flatten.description:
Flatten nested objects into a single level with configurable key separators.

## Example
```yaml
flatten:
  key_separator: .    # Separator for nested keys
  prefix: user        # Optional prefix for all keys
  target: .data       # Path to nested object
```

b64_decode.description:
Decode a Base64-encoded string.

## Example
```yaml
b64_decode: .encoded_data    # Path to Base64 string
```

b64_decode_as_json.description:
Decode a Base64-encoded string and parse as JSON.

## Example
```yaml
b64_decode_as_json: .payload    # Path to Base64-encoded JSON
```

b64_encode.description:
Encode a value to Base64. Can be a direct string or custom transform configuration.

## Example
```yaml
b64_encode: .data    # Path to value to encode
```

yaml_to_json.description:
Convert YAML-formatted string to JSON.

## Example
```yaml
yaml_to_json: .yaml_data    # Path to YAML string
```

parse_csv.description:
Parse a CSV string into an array of header-keyed row objects. Point it at the
CSV string in the action's data (e.g. the raw request body via
`input: a|raw_body|`, or fetched text).

## Example
```yaml
parse_csv: "$"                       # replace the root CSV string with the rows
# parse_csv: { json_path: "$", key: rows }   # put the rows array under `rows`
```

to_csv.description:
Serialize an array of row objects INTO a CSV string — the inverse of
`parse_csv`. Columns come from the first row's keys and every later row is
written in that same order. Pair it with an email attachment
(`encoding: utf8`) to send a report.

## Example
```yaml
to_csv: "$"                              # replace the root rows array with a CSV string
# to_csv: { json_path: "$", key: csv }   # put the CSV string under `csv`
```

nested_transforms.description:
Apply nested transforms to specific keys. Maps keys to arrays of transform operations.

## Example
```yaml
nested_transforms:
  items:                    # Transform each item in the 'items' array
    - remove_keys:
        - internal_id
    - rename_keys:
        user_name: name
```

math.description:
Perform mathematical operations on numeric values with expressions.

`target` is OPTIONAL and defaults to the root object — omit it to read and
write fields at the top level (as below). Inside an expression, reference a
field with the `target.` prefix; that prefix is the substitution token and is
resolved against the target object, so a bare `price` is left as-is and will
not resolve. Set `target:` only to scope to a nested object (e.g. `.data`).

## Example
```yaml
math:
  expressions:                     # key = output field name
    total: target.price * target.quantity
    discounted: target.total * 0.9
  decimal_places: 2                # optional: round to 2 places (half away from zero)
  to_string: true                  # optional: render as text, keeping trailing zeros
```

aggregate.description:
Reduce a JSON array to a summary (sum/avg/min/max/count), optionally grouped.

## Example
```yaml
aggregate: { over: body.data, sum: [amount], count: true, group_by: [status] }
```

filter.description:
Filter array elements based on specified conditions.

## Example
```yaml
filter:
  target: .users                   # Path to array to filter
  conditions:
    .age:
      is_greater_than: 18
    .status:
      is_equal_to: "active"
```

generate_bytes.description:
Generate random bytes with specified length.

## Example
```yaml
generate_bytes:
  key: api_key      # Output key for generated bytes
  length: 32        # Number of bytes to generate
```

encrypt_value.description:
Encrypt a value using AES-256-GCM encryption.

## Example
```yaml
encrypt_value:
  key: encrypted_data           # Output key for encrypted result
  data: .sensitive_value        # Path to value to encrypt
  secret_key: a|var::ENCRYPTED_ENCRYPTION_KEY|  # Encryption key (must be encrypted variable)
  nonce: a|var::NONCE|          # Unique nonce (must be encrypted variable)
```

**Security:**
- Store encryption keys as encrypted AirPipe variables
- Use unique nonce values for each encryption operation

hmac.description:
Compute an HMAC of a message — the signing counterpart to the
`is_valid_hmac` assertion. Use it to sign webhook deliveries you SEND,
then interpolate the result into a header.

## Example
```yaml
hmac:
  key: signature                  # Output key for the digest
  data: a|BuildPayload::body|     # The message to sign
  secret: a|Subscriber::secret|   # Per-recipient signing secret
  algorithm: sha256               # sha1 | sha256 (default) | sha512
  encoding: hex                   # hex (default) | base64
```

A digest produced here verifies under `is_valid_hmac` with the same
`algorithm` and `encoding`.

decrypt_value.description:
Decrypt a value previously sealed with `encrypt_value` (AES-256-GCM).

## Example
```yaml
decrypt_value:
  key: plaintext                # Output key for the decrypted string
  value: a|Row::enc_value|      # Base64 ciphertext (the encrypt_value `.value`)
  nonce: a|Row::enc_nonce|      # Base64 nonce   (the encrypt_value `.nonce`)
  tag: a|Row::enc_tag|          # Base64 GCM tag (the encrypt_value `.tag`)
  secret_key: a|env::AIRPIPE_ENC_SECRET_KEY|  # Same key used to encrypt
```

**Security:** decryption is authenticated — a wrong key, altered ciphertext,
or altered tag fails loudly rather than returning garbage.

s3_generate_presigned_url.description:
Generate a presigned URL for S3 file access.

## Example
```yaml
s3_generate_presigned_url:
  bucket: my-bucket                         # S3 bucket name
  file_key: documents/file.pdf              # Path to file in bucket
  expiration_secs: 3600                     # URL expiration (seconds)
  endpoint: https://s3.amazonaws.com        # S3 endpoint
  region: us-east-1                         # AWS region
  access_key_id: a|var::ENCRYPTED_AWS_ACCESS_KEY|  # AWS access key (encrypted variable)
  secret_access_key: a|var::ENCRYPTED_AWS_SECRET|  # AWS secret key (encrypted variable)
  key: presigned_url                        # Output key for generated URL
  json_path: .file_url                      # Optional: Extract from response
```

**Security:** Store AWS credentials securely as encrypted AirPipe variables:
```yaml
access_key_id: a|var::ENCRYPTED_AWS_ACCESS_KEY|
secret_access_key: a|var::ENCRYPTED_AWS_SECRET|
```

from.description: The JSON path to the starting array

paths.description: Array of JSON paths to extract values from each element

value.description:
JSON path to the HTML string within the action's data. An empty string means the
data IS the HTML — which is what an http action fetching a page gives you.

selector.description:
A CSS selector, the same grammar a browser takes: `article h2.title`,
`a[href^="/docs"]`, `tr td:nth-child(2)`.

key.description: Key to write the result under.

attribute.description:
Take this attribute from each matched element instead of its text. An element that
matches but lacks the attribute contributes `null`, so an `all: true` result stays
index-aligned with the elements on the page.

html.description:
Take each matched element's inner HTML instead of its text. Mutually exclusive with
`attribute`.

all.description:
Every match, as an array. Without it, the first match alone — or `null` when the
selector matched nothing.

value.description:
JSON path to the value to compress. An empty string means the whole action data.
A non-string value is compressed as its compact JSON.

key.description: Key to write the compressed text under.

encoding.description: How to render the compressed bytes as text: `base64` (default), `base64url`, `hex`.

level.description:
0 (store) to 9 (smallest). Default 6 — zlib's own default, and the point past which
more CPU stops buying much.

value.description: JSON path to the compressed text.

key.description: Key to write the decompressed value under.

algorithm.description: `gzip` (default), `zlib`, or `deflate`. Must match how it was compressed.

encoding.description:
How the text is encoded: `base64` (default), `base64url`, `hex`. The two base64
alphabets are accepted interchangeably, so a value that lost its padding crossing a
URL still decodes.

json.description: Parse the result as JSON instead of keeping it as text.

secret.description: The shared secret, base32 by default.

key.description: Key to write the generated code under.

value.description: JSON path to the base64 of the workbook. An empty string means the whole action data.

key.description: Key to write the rows under.

sheet.description: Sheet name. The first sheet when omitted.

headers.description:
Treat the first row as column names, so each later row becomes an object. Default
true. Set false when the first row is data and every row should be an array.

limit.description:
Rows to read. Default 10000 — a sheet can hold a million, and returning all of them
as JSON is never what a caller wanted.

encoding.description: How the file is encoded: `base64` (default) or `base64url`.

value.description: JSON path to the base64 of the PDF. An empty string means the whole action data.

key.description: Key to write the extracted text under.

encoding.description: How the file is encoded: `base64` (default) or `base64url`.

target.description: Where to apply the expressions (JSONPath). Defaults to the root.

expressions.description: Output field name → expression, e.g. `total: target.price * target.quantity`.

to_string.description:
Render the result as a string. With `decimal_places` this keeps trailing zeros —
`10.00` rather than `10` — which is what a money value usually wants to look like.

decimal_places.description:
Round the result to this many decimal places, half away from zero (2.125 → 2.13).
The value stays a NUMBER unless `to_string` (or `eval_type: string`) asks for text.

eval_type.description:
Force the result type. `decimal_places` applies to any float result on its own; this
is for coercing (e.g. `int` to truncate).

TransformAggregate.description: Reduce a JSON array to a summary (sum / avg / min / max / count), optionally grouped.

over.description:
JSONPath to the array to aggregate. Omit to aggregate the whole data when it is
itself an array.

key.description: Output field to hold the summary. Omit to replace the data with the summary.

min.description: Fields to take the minimum of.

max.description: Fields to take the maximum of.

count.description: Include a row count in the summary (default true when no other op is given).

group_by.description: Group rows by these fields; the summary is computed per group under `groups`.

conditions.description: Conditions to filter items in the array.

HmacSign.description:
Parameters for the `hmac` post-transform (signing).

## Example
```yaml
hmac:
  key: signature
  data: a|BuildPayload::body|
  secret: a|Subscriber::secret|
  algorithm: sha256
  encoding: hex
```

key.description: Output key the computed digest is written to.

data.description: The message to sign. Supports interpolation.

secret.description:
The signing secret. Supports interpolation — use `a|ap_var::NAME|` or a
per-recipient secret read from a prior action.

operation.description:
`get` (default) mints a time-limited DOWNLOAD link; `put` mints a time-limited
UPLOAD target the client can PUT straight to, so the file never transits AirPipe.

database.description:
Database name on the connection — the Mongo/Cosmos/DocumentDB database, not the
`database:` key of the action, which names the *connection* in `global.databases`.

operation.description:
Which operation to perform.

The engine dispatches on this string, and an unrecognised value fails the action
rather than defaulting to anything. Supported:
`find`, `findOne`, `findOneAndDelete`, `findOneAndReplace`, `insertOne`,
`insertMany`, `updateOne`, `updateMany`, `deleteOne`, `deleteMany`, `aggregate`.

filter.description:
Query selector, for the read, update and delete operations.

```yaml
filter: '{"email": "a|body::email|"}'
```

pipeline.description: Stages for `aggregate`. Ignored by every other operation.

delete.description: Reserved for delete payloads; `filter` selects what a delete removes.

update.description:
Update document, for `updateOne` and `updateMany` — including its operators, e.g.
`{"$set": {...}}`.

options.description:
Driver options passed through for this operation, such as `projection`, `sort`,
`limit` or `upsert`. Which keys apply depends on the operation.

Param.description:
Parameter definition for interface-level URL parameters with optional
validation and default values.

## Example
```yaml
interfaces:
  getUser:
    method: GET
    params:
      id:
        value: a|params::id|
        error_message: "User ID is required"
        validate:
          is_not_empty: true
          regex: "^[0-9]+$"
      page:
        value: a|params::page|
        default_value: "1"
```

default_value.description: Default value if the parameter is not provided.

error_message.description: Custom error message when validation fails.

validate.description:
Validation test to run against the parameter value.

## Example
```yaml
validate:
  is_not_empty: true
  is_less_than: 100
  regex: "^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$"
```

InterfaceContract.description:
What an interface accepts or returns, as a contract: a shape and an example of it.

One type for both directions so the two sides stay symmetric, and named for what an
interface does rather than for HTTP: interfaces are also MQTT subscriptions, WebSocket
channels, MCP tools and cron schedules, and only one of those has a "request".

Before this, the inbound side had a derived schema plus a flat `request_example` and
the outbound side had only a flat `response_example` — two different shapes for the
same idea, and 299 hand-written examples across the marketplace packs that nothing
validated against reality.

Both fields are optional: the schema is derived when it can be, and the example is
best produced by promoting a recorded run rather than typing one out.

schema.description: JSON Schema for this side of the call. Derived from assertions when omitted.

example.description: A representative payload, shown in the generated docs.

NetworkPolicy.description:
Network access-control policy. Set it config-wide (top-level `network:`, applies
to every interface as a baseline) and/or per-interface (`interface.network:`,
which inherits and **tightens** the config-wide policy).

## Inheritance (tighten-only)
- `deny` lists (ip/geo/asn) **union** across levels — a config-level deny can
  never be weakened by an interface.
- `allow` lists **intersect** — the request must satisfy every level that
  declares an allow list.
- An interface sets `inherit: false` to ignore the config-wide policy entirely
  (a deliberate public exception, e.g. a health route).
- Scalar settings (`mode`, `source`, `trusted_proxies`, `on_deny`) are taken
  from the interface when present, otherwise inherited from the config level.

## Evaluation order (per level)
`ip.deny` → `geo.deny` → `asn.deny` → `*.allow` → `rate_limit`. The first rule
that rejects wins. In `monitor` mode nothing is blocked; matches are logged.

## Example
```yaml
network:                       # config-wide baseline
  mode: enforce                # enforce (default) | monitor
  source: client               # client (default) | socket | real_ip
  trusted_proxies:             # validate XFF chain (anti-spoofing)
    - "10.0.0.0/8"
  ip:
    allow: ["203.0.113.0/24", "2001:db8::/32"]
    deny:  ["1.2.3.4"]
    deny_check: source         # source (default) | all
  geo:   { deny: ["RU", "KP"] }
  asn:   { deny: [13335] }
  rate_limit: { per: ip, requests: 100, window: "60s" }
  on_deny: { status: 403, body: { error: "forbidden" } }

interfaces:
  admin:
    network:                   # inherits + tightens the baseline
      ip: { allow: ["198.51.100.10"] }
  health:
    network: { inherit: false } # public exception
```

inherit.description:
Interface-level only: when `false`, ignore the config-wide policy for this
interface. Defaults to `true`. Ignored at the config level.

source.description: Which captured IP to treat as authoritative. Defaults to `client`.

trusted_proxies.description:
Trusted proxy CIDRs. When set, the client IP is resolved by walking the
`X-Forwarded-For` chain from the right and skipping these hops, which
defeats client-supplied header spoofing. Without it, `source: client`
trusts the leftmost (spoofable) XFF entry.

geo.description: Country-level allow/deny rules (requires a GeoIP provider).

asn.description: ASN allow/deny rules (requires an ASN provider).

on_deny.description: Response to return when a request is denied in `enforce` mode.

NetworkMode.description: Operating mode for a [`NetworkPolicy`]. Defaults to `enforce`.

oneOf.description: Block requests that fail any rule, returning the `on_deny` response. Default.

Never block. Evaluate every rule and log what *would* have been blocked.
Use this to validate a policy against live traffic before enforcing it
(equivalent to a WAF "count"/"log-only" mode).

IpFilterSource.description:
Which IP field from the incoming request is used as the authoritative source
when evaluating `allow` and `deny` rules in an [`IpRule`].

Defaults to `client` when not specified.

oneOf.description: Leftmost X-Forwarded-For entry (best-guess real client). Default.
Raw TCP socket peer address (reliable when no proxy is involved).
X-Real-IP header value, falling back to `client` if not present.

allow.description:
Allowed IPs / CIDR ranges. If set, only matching requests pass (evaluated
against the policy `source` IP). Across levels these intersect.

deny.description:
Blocked IPs / CIDR ranges. Matching requests are denied. Across levels these
union (a config-level deny always applies). `deny_check` controls scope.

deny_check.description:
Which IPs are checked against `deny`: `source` (default) checks only the
resolved source IP; `all` checks every IP in the request chain.

DenyCheckMode.description:
Controls which IPs are checked against the `deny` list.

Defaults to `source` when not specified.

oneOf.description: Only check the configured `source` IP against the deny list. Default.

Check deny rules against every IP in the full chain: client, socket,
X-Real-IP, and all X-Forwarded-For hops. Useful for blocking known bad
actors even when they route through proxies.

GeoRule.description:
Country-level (GeoIP) allow/deny rule. Requires a configured GeoIP provider.
Country codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (e.g. "US", "GB"), case-insensitive.

allow.description: Allowed country codes. If set, only requests resolving to one of these pass.

deny.description: Denied country codes. Requests resolving to one of these are blocked.

require_resolution.description:
When the country cannot be resolved: `true` blocks (fail-closed), `false`
(default) skips the rule (fail-open).

AsnRule.description: Autonomous System Number allow/deny rule. Requires a configured ASN provider.

allow.description: Allowed ASNs. If set, only requests resolving to one of these pass.

deny.description: Denied ASNs. Requests resolving to one of these are blocked.

require_resolution.description: When the ASN cannot be resolved: `true` blocks, `false` (default) skips.

RateLimitRule.description: Per-identifier request rate limit using a sliding window.

per.description: What to bucket requests by. Defaults to `ip`.

window.description: Window length as a humantime string ("60s", "1m", "1h"). Defaults to "60s".

burst.description:
Optional short-term burst allowance above `requests`. Reserved for the
token-bucket backend; ignored by the sliding-window default.

RateLimitScope.description: Identifier a [`RateLimitRule`] buckets requests by. Defaults to `ip`.

oneOf.description: Bucket by the policy's resolved `source` IP address. Default.

DenyResponse.description: Response returned when a request is denied in `enforce` mode.

status.description: HTTP status code. Defaults to 403. Set to 404 to hide a route's existence.

headers.description: Extra response headers to attach (e.g. `Retry-After` for rate limits).

McpTool.description:
Opt-in MCP tool exposure for an interface. See [`Interface::mcp`].

The MCP server auto-generates the tool's `inputSchema` from the interface's
`assert` tests (the same schema that powers the OpenAPI docs), so no separate
schema needs to be authored here.

enabled.description: Expose this interface as an MCP tool. Default `false`.

tool_name.description: Override the tool name shown to MCP clients. Defaults to the interface name.

description.description: Override the tool description. Defaults to the interface `summary`/`description`.

list_authorizer.description:
Optional per-tool `tools/list` authorizer: the name of an interface in this config that is
RUN (with the forwarded request headers) when a client lists tools. The tool appears in the
listing only if that interface returns success (2xx). Absent = the tool is public discovery.

This is how a customer gates DISCOVERY with their OWN auth: `tools/list` executes no actions,
so the interface-level auth that protects `tools/call` never runs for it. The authorizer is a
normal interface (e.g. a `ValidateJwt` action asserting `is_valid_jwt` against the customer's
secret, plus any org/role checks); the managed MCP handler runs it and hides the tool on
failure. See `airpipe-http-server/src/mcp_managed.rs`.

server.description:
Which declared MCP server this tool belongs to (see [`IntegrationConfig::mcp_servers`]).
Omitted = the default server, which is what every pre-existing config gets.

The id may be declared in a *different* config in the same org+environment: an MCP server is
a named group of tools, not a property of one config, so many configs can contribute tools to
one server. A id that resolves to no declaration is a configuration error and the tool is
omitted from every server rather than published onto the wrong one.

synchronous.description:
SQLite-only: `PRAGMA synchronous` (`OFF` | `NORMAL` | `FULL` | `EXTRA`). Defaults to `NORMAL`
(with WAL journaling) when unset — durable against application/process crashes and ~10x faster
than `FULL` on writes. Set `FULL`/`EXTRA` for maximum durability, or `OFF` for maximum speed
(no crash durability). Ignored by non-SQLite drivers.

McpServer.description:
A named MCP server: an identity, plus the tools that join it by id.

Declared under [`IntegrationConfig::mcp_servers`] and joined by [`McpTool::server`]. Declaring
and contributing are deliberately separate. Air Pipe's own management MCP is assembled from many
configs but is one server with one identity, so repeating the identity in each contributing
config would leave no single source of truth; conversely one org may publish several distinct
MCP offerings from different subsets of its configs.

`title` and `instructions` exist because MCP registries (mcp.so, Glama, Smithery, PulseMCP) read
a remote server's listing metadata straight off the `initialize` response — there is no separate
place to write a description. Without them a listing renders as a bare name and a wall of tool
descriptions.

title.description:
Display name shown to MCP clients and registries (`serverInfo.title`).
Absent = clients fall back to the protocol-level server name.

instructions.description:
Server-level description, emitted as the `initialize` result's `instructions`.
This is the field MCP registries surface as the listing description.

default.description:
Serve this identity on the bare `/<org>/<env>/mcp` route, i.e. adopt the tools that name no
server. At most one per org+environment; ties resolve deterministically by config name.

OnError.description:
A handler that runs when a run of this config fails.

It runs **after** the response has been decided and is never awaited, so it cannot add
latency to the request that failed, and its own failure cannot change what the caller
received. A handler that fails is logged and dropped.

interface.description:
Name of an interface in this config to run. It receives a JSON body describing
what failed:

```json
{
  "config": "orders-api",
  "interface": "CreateOrder",
  "http_code": 500,
  "run_uuid": "0199...",
  "at": "2026-08-22T04:15:00Z",
  "data": { }
}
```

so a handler reads `a|body->interface|`, `a|body->http_code|` and the rest.

status.description:
Which status codes count as a failure worth handling. Defaults to any non-2xx.

## Example
```yaml
status: [500, 502, 503, 504]
```

max_per_minute.description:
The most handler runs to start in any one minute, per config. Defaults to 12.

This is a guard, not a tuning knob. An error handler that fires per request turns
an outage into a second outage: every failing request would start another run,
against a dependency that is already unhealthy, and bill for it. Beyond the limit
the failure is still counted and logged — only the handler is skipped.

## Example
```yaml
max_per_minute: 6
```
